codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of the QEMU Wasm build pipeline and custom Emscripten display backend. The Dockerfile is a well-structured 297-line multi-stage build that cross-compiles all dependencies (zlib, libffi, GLib, Pixman) and QEMU with correct Emscripten flags. The display backend (build/emscripten.c, 297 lines) properly implements DisplayChangeListener with dpy_gfx_update/switch/refresh callbacks, exports 10 EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE functions for framebuffer access, keyboard input (PS/2 scancodes), and both relative and absolute mouse input. Build artifacts verified: 40.5MB .wasm, 272KB .js glue, 4 BIOS ROMs. All expected behaviors met. EMSDK version was changed from 3.1.50 to 4.0.10 (matching container2wasm reference), which is a well-justified deviation documented in the handoff. Three source patches for Emscripten 4.x compatibility are correctly applied.

issues.description: qemu_display_check_dirty() has a non-atomic read-and-clear race: if QEMU thread sets fb_dirty=1 between the if-check and the fb_dirty=0 clear, one frame update notification is lost. In practice this is inconsequential — the polling loop (30ms setInterval) will catch it on the next iteration — but using __atomic_exchange would be strictly correct.

Shared framebuffer state uses 'volatile' for cross-thread visibility. While volatile is not a proper synchronization mechanism in C11, in the Emscripten/Wasm context with simple 32-bit aligned reads/writes and the polling pattern, this is functionally adequate. C11 _Atomic or __atomic builtins would be more correct but are not required for this use case.
qemu_display_data() casts away volatile qualifier: (uint8_t *)exported_fb_ptr. This is technically undefined behavior in C but is benign in the Emscripten/Wasm memory model.

KEEPALIVE count check uses grep -c which counts all string occurrences (13, including 3 in comments), not just function decorators (10). The threshold of >= 6 is still correct, but the handoff's claim of '13 KEEPALIVE exports' is slightly misleading — there are 10 exported functions. Cosmetic issue only.

The actual approach is cleaner (avoids duplicating the full QEMU source tree in the repo) but the convention of where C sources live should be noted.
